system_prompt_style.note: Prompts are text templates filled via generate_prompt with persona variables; no single persistent system prompt.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: we represent the sandbox environment—areas and objects—as a tree data structure
env_context_strategy.note: Agent's spatial memory tree is flattened into natural language and injected into prompts.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: The top-ranked memories that fit within the language model’s context window are included in the prompt.
context_compaction.note: Reflections summarize memories; retrieval limits what enters the prompt rather than sending full history.

observation_format.evidence_quote: Everything in the architecture is recorded and reasoned over as a natural language description

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: the agents output a natural language statement describing their current action
tool_call_format.note: No tool-call API; outputs are free text parsed by __func_clean_up functions. Closest value; actually 'natural-language-parsed', see Ambiguities.

tool_count.note: No tool schemas are exposed; the model only completes prompts.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: The agents interact with the world by their actions, and with each other through natural language.
edit_primitive.note: No file-editing capability; agents act in a sandbox game world.

tool_schema_source.note: No tool schemas at all; hand-written prompt templates are the nearest analogue.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: To set up your environment, you will need to generate a `utils.py` file that contains your OpenAI API key
protocol_standardization.note: Direct OpenAI API only; no MCP/A2A in repo evidence.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: Generative agents operate in an action loop where, at each time step, they perceive the world around them and those perceived observations are stored in their memory stream.
loop_primitives.note: Plan is generated top-down then executed and revised; perception-action loop each step.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: our approach starts top-down and then recursively generates more detail
planning_granularity.note: Daily plan -> hourly chunks -> 5-15 minute chunks, stored in memory stream.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: Agents communicate with each other in full natural language. They are aware of other agents in their local area
multi_agent_topology.note: 25 equal agents in the default base simulation.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: the generative agent architecture determines whether they walk by or engage in conversation
delegation_mechanism.note: Agents converse but no work is delegated to another agent.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: To directly command one of the agents, the user takes on the persona of the agent’s “inner voice”
human_in_loop.note: Users steer via natural-language intervention and the `run <step-count>` prompt; not per-action approval. Closest values; see Ambiguities.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: A plan includes a location, a starting time, and a duration.
short_term_state.note: Persona has scratch (daily_req, schedule) plus memory structures.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: At the center of our architecture is the memory stream, a database that maintains a comprehensive record of an agent’s experience.
long_term_memory.note: embeddings.json stores memory embeddings used for relevance (associative_memory.py).

state_persistence.evidence_quote: This will allow you to restart your simulation from the point where you left off.

self_verification.evidence_quote:
What 5 high-level insights can you infer from
the above statements?
self_verification.note: Reflection is the agent reviewing its own memories; also __func_validate output validation per prompt.

retry_policy.note: 5 retries with a fail-safe fallback at the prompt level; no task-level attempts.

rollback.evidence_quote: exit the simulation without saving by typing `exit`, or save and exit by typing `fin`
rollback.note: Only save/discard of a whole simulation; no in-run revert mechanism found.

termination_condition.note: Simulation runs the requested number of game steps then returns to the prompt.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: Running these simulations, at least as of early 2023, could be somewhat costly
cost_controls.note: Cost is acknowledged but no budget, routing or caching mechanism is provided.

timeouts.evidence_quote: We've noticed that OpenAI's API can hang when it reaches the hourly rate limit. When this happens, you may need to restart your simulation.
timeouts.note: README explicitly says hangs require manual restart, i.e. no timeout.

execution_isolation.note: Runs in-process on the host; agent 'actions' occur in the Django sandbox world, not the OS.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: All simulations that you save will be located in `environment/frontend_server/storage`
filesystem_access.note: Agents have no filesystem tool at all; they act on a simulated world tree.

network_policy.evidence_quote:
# Copy and paste your OpenAI API Key
openai_api_key = "<Your OpenAI API>"
network_policy.note: No network restriction configuration; process calls OpenAI directly.

permission_model.evidence_quote: The agent’s output action then updates the JSON, and the process loops for the next time step.
permission_model.note: Model outputs are applied to the world with no authorisation check.

tracing.evidence_quote: The server maintains a JSON data structure that contains information about each agent in the sandbox world
tracing.note: Per-step simulation state saved to storage; verbose prompt printing via print_run_prompts when debug=True.

replayability.evidence_quote: You can replay a simulation that you have already run simply by having your environment server running
replayability.note: Replay is a visual playback of recorded steps, not model re-execution.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: It contains our core simulation module for  generative agents—computational agents that simulate believable human behaviors—and their game environment.
eval_hooks.note: Evaluation was human interviews described in the paper; no evaluation runner in the repo evidence.

guardrails.evidence_quote: the sandbox server parses the JSON for any changes coming from the generative agents, moves the agents to their new positions
guardrails.note: No filtering or action-blocking layer; paper Sec. on ethics recommends logging only.

target_domain.evidence_quote: computational software agents that simulate believable human behavior
target_domain.note: Domain is social simulation / believable agents in a sandbox game world.

open_source.evidence_quote: A public repository for the simulation code is located here: https://github.com/joonspk-research/generative_agents
open_source.note: License file not in the provided evidence.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: Our current implementation utilizes the gpt3.5-turbo version of ChatGPT
model_agnostic.note: Hard-coded OpenAI engines such as text-davinci-003 in gpt_param.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: This repository accompanies our research paper titled "[Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior]

first_release_date.note: No tag or release date in the provided evidence; paper published UIST '23.

pinned_version.note: Repo is untagged; pinned to main at the evidence date.
